intro_paragraphs: This questionnaire is meant as a tool to aide in roleplaying and character creation: to not see a character as a pile of numbers on a nicely-formatted spreadsheet, but to explain the all-important who they are and why they are who they say they are.

It is not mandatory. However, it is strongly recommended, as it will give you (and me, the DM) a better grasp on your character, and I will be working off of your character backstory based on the information given. Write me a novella if you feel like - the more information you give, the better. That said, don’t stress over it if you don’t want to fill out everything or if you get stuck. I recommend skipping to the questions you find most interesting.

You also do not have to answer any questions you’re uncomfortable with, particularly the ones related to sex (question 13). Again, this questionnaire was written in large part by someone else, who may have had a different group dynamic and play-style than we might have.

As regards how the questionnaire is answered, that is up to you. I’ve followed the original questionnaire author’s advice and answered my character questionnaires in the first person as the character, if they were given that questionnaire -- unless the character wouldn’t know the answer, in which case I answer in the omniscient narrative form, or write down the pertinent information separately.

That said, let’s dive right in. Please, copy this document and edit your copy as much as you like. Or, alternatively, I can hand you an example of one I filled out for a character not involved in your campaign, if you want to see how I did this.

This questionnaire was primarily originally written by ShadowDragon8685, and has since seen some edits. Primary credit for all verbiage in this document goes to him. (See also the preserved attribution notice at the end of the document.)
appendix_notice: [This is an appendix containing questions that were worth putting a content warning on; however, entirely blotting them out of the original questionnaire author’s work felt inappropriate to the spirit of not concealing or making light of grislier parts of the setting.

As a reminder, I will follow player comfort about any topics that may be uncomfortable or difficult; and, also, as a reminder, the original verbiage of these questions comes from the original author of the questionnaire, and I may have missed something while looking over them (and didn’t know what was the best approach with others). While that applies to the entirety of this questionnaire, it is worth bringing up again because I didn’t exactly like the way the original introduced several of these.
If you would like, copy the text of these questions and your answers back into the main body of the sheet, and/or delete this section.

chapters.title: Fall, Origin, Morph, Home & Livelihood
chapters.description: Introduce your ego to the post-Fall solar system: where you were during the Fall, how you came into being, what sleeve you wear today, where you return, and how you survive.

chapters.title: Politics & Polarizing Entities
chapters.description: Where do you stand politically, and how do you view the major polities, coalitions, and clandestine forces of the system?

chapters.title: Polarizing Setting Issues
chapters.description: From indenture and uplifts to forking, resleeving, indefinite lifespans, and psi — explore the social fault lines of transhumanity.

chapters.title: Contacts, Uniqueness, Quirks & Minor Motivators
chapters.description: Who stays constant in your life, what truly distinguishes you beyond your C.V., what weirdnesses define you, and what smaller causes move you.

chapters.title: Rapid-Fire Profile
chapters.description: A question will be furnished with little, if any, explanation. Answer as you see fit.

chapters.title: About Your Muse
chapters.description: Almost everybody has one: your muse's demeanor, avatar, skills, and the biggest disagreement between you.

chapters.title: Gender, Sex & Relationships
chapters.description: Optional, encouraged, and configurable to player comfort. Explore gender identity (13a–13b) and optional sexuality/experience sections (13c, 13e).

chapters.title: Recreation, Frivolities, Emotion & Trauma
chapters.description: Music, gaming, skinning, hobbies, and substances alongside death, fear, anger, betrayal, and loss.

chapters.title: Exosolar Affairs
chapters.description: Pandora's Gate yawns open wide: gatecrashing, exosolar ecology, and alien contact.

questions.heading: How did the Fall affect you, and where were you when it happened?
questions.primer: It was only a decade ago, but were you even around at the time, or did you come into being afterwards? Do you vividly remember it, or was it largely something that happened to other people far, far away from you? Or is it a mysterious gap in your memories?

questions.heading: How did you come into being?
questions.primer: Most people these days aren’t in the body they were born in, if they were even “born” at all; conversely, some who were not born, in the traditional sense, occupy bodies. So, what’s your origin story?

questions.heading: What are you now?
questions.primer: Unless you’re one of those super-rare people who still have their original bodies, you’ve resleeved or egocast at least once. What changed in the process - did you go from being a relatively normal human female to a clanking, genderless synthetic; or perhaps come into being as an infolife being, but have since decided to sleeve into a male neo-bonobo? The possibilities are nearly as limitless as human creativity.

questions.heading: Where do you live or come back to?
questions.primer: Transhumans live in a lot of places, throughout the solar system and beyond, but almost all of them have a “home,” even the ones who live on Scum barges floating perpetually throughout the solar system. Very few people are professional drifters without any sort of roots or home base whatsoever.

questions.heading: What do you do?
questions.primer: Most people do something to earn a living, even if there’s no monetary exchanges involved in their lives. Are you an old-school mechanic who can make any two pieces of junk work together, a nano-engineer who programs cornucopia machines with fabrication blueprints, a cool hunter, a gene hacker, a taxi driver? If you live on an anarcho-collectivist habitat and consequently don’t have any wage-slavery forcing you to do something to make ends meet (because ends meet automatically), what do you do with your time, for your hab, what keeps your rep score high, et cetera?

questions.heading: Where do you stand, politically?
questions.primer: Poll any ten transhumans about politics and you’ll get eleven opinions: which is yours? Do you like the Planetary Consortium or other hypercorp-ruled territories, are you down with Titanian Technosocialism, are you an Anarcho-collectivist, are you an Argonaut who’s turned science into a cause and stay out of politics altogether? Are you Scum who lives for the now, doesn’t give a flying fuck about the politics; a neo-primitivist; a hardcore Mercurial, heavily active in the Synth Rights movement? Do you think everyone should be be allowed to choose the political system that applies to them, as the Anarchists do? And given where you stand politically and where you live geospatially, is there friction between you and the locals? If you’re one of the clanking masses on Luna or a marginalized Barsoomian on Mars, you might well feel at odds with the reigning powers - or you might be a member of one of the Oligarch street gangs on Titan who do not hold to Technosocialism and feel that everybody should be left to sink or swim monetarily on their own merits.

questions.heading: I’m going to name some particularly polarizing political entities.
questions.primer: You may not have a particularly strong opinion on all of them, but if you don’t have an opinion on any of them, you seem awfully apathetic about the ‘verse...

questions.heading: The Morningstar Constellation
questions.primer: A breakaway faction from the PC, the Constellation was formed by the combination of Venusian terraformers who wanted to engage in “High-Altitude Terraformation” and continue building habitable aerostats and Venusian independance agitators. Do you support their breakaway from the Planetary Consortium, or view them as upstart secessionists who will soon be brought back into the fold, hat-in-hand?

questions.heading: The Lunar-Lagrange Alliance
questions.primer: The LLA was the rising star in exoatmospheric power blocs in the days before the Fall, but after those on Earth itself (which did not survive the Fall), the LLA took the brunt of it. They nonetheless continue to host most of the respectable in-system banks. Do you support the LLA’s return to power, or think the PC should move in and take over Luna and the remaining orbital habs the LLA currently exists in? Or do you have an alternative view on the topic?

questions.heading: The Reclamation of Earth
questions.primer: It’s no secret that the Planetary Consortium would just as soon that everybody forgot Earth and its cultures and governments existed. Most folks have views on this topic, one way or another. What’s your view, and why? Do you think that what’s buried on Earth might be best left on Earth, or are you in a hurry to dig up and expose the horrors of the Fall and the evacuations thereof?

questions.heading: The Planetary Consortium
questions.primer: The biggest power in the system in terms of number of instantiated egos under their sway, the PC is the 900-lb gorilla champion of hypercorporate domination over all other spheres of life, who have no problem moving in and taking what they want by force, because nobody can stop them (except when they do). A lot of people want to see them crumble, but an awful lot call the PC home. Where do you stand, and is your skin in the game, or are you watching from afar?

questions.heading: The Jovian Republic
questions.primer: Known to its detractors as the Jovian Junta, everyone outside the Republic itself refers to it as such, given that it descended from actual military juntas on Earth and used force to lay claim to everything in Jupiter’s orbit. In the eyes of most others in the system, it is a fascist, bioconservative, technophobic police state. Yet to its inhabitants, it is the only sane faction in a system full of people who abandoned their humanity. A broad swath of the system hates them, whether they are actively vested in doing them harm, or would just cheer from the sidelines if a wave of antimatter missiles and relativistic kill vehicles wiped them off of Jupiter’s orbit. Other detractors pity the Jovian citizens and wish to liberate them from the government. Others still mostly just want to avoid ever having to think about them. Where do you stand?

questions.heading: The Autonomist Alliance
questions.primer: There was a time when the various powers rimward of the asteroid belt were isolated and vulnerable; even the Titanian Commonwealth was a small-fry compared to the PC, with an order of magnitude fewer citizens. Then the Points of Unity were declared, habitats and even the Titanian Commonwealth declared adherence to them, and they received their baptism-by-fire when the PC twice attempted to invade Locus and the Alliance beat them like an anvil both times. How do you feel about the Autonomist Alliance - are you active in political speech within it, or do you see it all as a bunch of rebels and anarchists, or what?

questions.heading: The Titanian Commonwealth
questions.primer: The Titanians missed out on the First Battle of Locus, being a statist entity amongst a loose coalition of entities who almost universally appeared to be hostile to statism, but when the PC made it clear they intended to expand their dominion across the solar system, the Titanians knew that they would be the ones conquered after the anarchists, and joined the Second Battle of Locus guns blazing. They remain the odd-man-out, being the only statist polity in the Alliance. Whether inside or outside the AA, you probably have an opinion on the Titanians and their technosocialism.

questions.heading: Anarcho-Collectivism
questions.primer: The heart and soul of the Autonomist Alliance, anarcho-collectivists are by no means a unified lot. What they all agree upon, however, is that nobody has the right to tell anybody what to do without that anybody’s say in the matter. Their detractors call them, well, anarchists, and argue that anarcho-collectivism is unsustainable and will quickly devolve into the eating-itself-alive, war-of-all-against-all, violence-rape-and-murder kind of anarchy that the word conjures in the heads of more traditionally-minded folk.

questions.heading: Extropians
questions.primer: Many, some would say most, of those who hold to the Autonomist Alliance Points of Unity, would consider Anarcho-Capitalism to be even more of the odd-man-out than the Titanian Commonwealth. The Extropians narrowly avoided being expelled from the Alliance in a vote not too long ago, as the overwhelming opinion is that their continued practice of indenture amounts to the same sort of slavery the Planetary Consortium, LLA and Morningstar Alliance practice, and more and more Autonomists are coming to the conclusion that indenture practices are the inevitable result of capitalism in any form. Extropians, of course, defend these practices, saying that nobody is coerced into doing anything, a claim which the most vocal Autonomists deride as utterly ludicrous. Where do you stand?

questions.heading: The Scum.
questions.primer: Wearing the title as a point of pride, most Scum live in “Barges” which are part of Fleets, floating in orbits around the solar system, doing business where they are. Some see them as modern-day gypsies, and they aren’t wrong, given that Scum hold their first and often only loyalty to themselves, their own Barge, and the Swarm, in that order. Scum live for the now, and most don’t give one solitary fuck about continual scientific or sociological progress unless it advances the cause of better scum life and more creative hedonism; for the most part, they feel that humanity should just live for pleasure from now until the heat-death of the universe.

questions.heading: The Argonauts
questions.primer: An ostensibly apolitical organization dedicated to the cause of Science, the argonauts have found themselves a de facto political cause, given that many of the tenets they hold true are some which major polities object to. The Argonauts believe that all information should be open and free, and are heavy movers in the open-source community. Some say the Argonauts should bite the bullet and declare adherence to the Points of Unity, others vehemently insist the Argonauts remain strictly apolitical, and of course, there is always the pressure of publish or die.

questions.heading: The Ultimates
questions.primer: When most people think of the Ultimates, they think of mercenaries. While this is true, in the sense that many, if not most, Ultimates are mercenaries, and you can still hire the organization as a whole if you have the credit or resources to offer, this is a dangerous generalization of the entire purpose of the Ultimates. In fact, the Ultimates are strong proponents of a Darwinian view of transhuman evolution, only one step removed from Exhumans in that they believe in said Darwinian evolution of transhumanity, not leaving humanity behind altogether. The Ultimates are the biggest single power rimward of Titan, and while they sell their services as mercenaries, everyone in their right mind would do well to remember that the Ultimates are, ultimately, for the Ultimates, not for their employers.

questions.heading: Exhumans and Singularity Seekers
questions.primer: Exhumans are those who want to leave all vestiges of transhumanity behind; to become something other, something “greater,” or at least utterly alien. The single factor that unites all things classified as exhumans and distinguishing them from, say, especially weird Brinkers and Isolates, is that they are a threat to transhumanity, actively engaged in efforts either to destroy it, assimilate it, or outbreed it. Many exhumans are also singularity seekers, but not all singularity seekers are exhumans, though they’re often lumped together, including in this questionnaire. Singularity Seekers see the hard takeoff Singularity that the Titans underwent, the recursive self-improvement cycle that took them from merely being AGI software in impressive hardware to the all-consuming mechanical gods that nearly wiped out all of Transhumanity... and they want a part of it.

questions.heading: The TITANs
questions.primer: It’s fair to say that almost everybody has a very negative opinion on the TITANs, even more than have a negative view of the Jovian Junta. Some live their entire lives in fear of the day the TITANs return to finish the job, others have chalked the TITANs into the “not worth worrying about” category, either because they feel that if the TITANs return there will be no stopping them, or because they feel they left the rest of Transhumanity alone because they no longer factored into the TITANs’ plans one way or another. (Advisory: if you change the font in your copy of the questionnaire and delete the expository paragraphs, show your GM and they may give you a point of Rez just for starting on the questionnaire.) There are some weirdos, primarily Singularity Seekers, who have a positive view of them and want to become them, and some Ultimates are ambivalent about the TITANs themselves, seeing them as the Darwinian evolutionary event which put the entirety of Transhumanity through an evolutionary crucible of fire and weeded out the deserving from the weak. Where do you stand?

questions.heading: Firewall
questions.primer: Seeing as Firewall is a clandestine agency who deliberately obscure themselves from public view, most people will never have heard of them at all. Others might think they are an urban legend, or a conspiracy theory. Anyone who has been used as an asset may have dealt with agents of Firewall without knowing it. Among those who have dealt with Firewall directly, opinions vary wildly: some think they’re unsung heroes transhumanity needs to survive; others would call them a misfortune upon anyone they meet, and would avoid dealing with them; others still would actively take a swing at them if they had the chance. Not many would object to their core mission of saving transhumanity from existential risks, but do their ends justify their means?

questions.heading: Some polarizing issues, which are different from polarizing politics, per se. Again: Where do you stand?
questions.primer: Feel free to write in general your feelings about polarizing issues. Or not!

questions.heading: Indenture
questions.primer: Touted by the PC, its biggest proponents, as the means by which those who have nothing, often not even a body, may work their way back into the economic system, indenture is universally reviled by everyone out-system that isn’t an Extropian as modern-day slavery, citing horrific (and in many cases, ongoing) abuses wherein the indentured person finds their indenture extended indefinitely due to tripping hidden penalty clauses in their massive contracts  or by being teased with goodies like simulspace vacations that add massive amounts of time to their indenture contracts.

questions.heading: Indenture contracts applied to minors
questions.primer: No, that’s not a typographical error. It’s a true fact; the PC and other indenture-using locations will quite happily let an 11-year-old ego sign away the next eight years of their life as a case-sleeved hard laborer or an infomorph secretary in exchange for the promise of an actual body. Even amongst folks who don’t care about indentured adults, this rubs them wrong. Others would argue that with muse assistance and the lack of any of that pesky biological growing stuff, a minor picks up the work easily and in an adult biomorph, a synthmorph, or as an infomorph, no-one can tell the difference anyway, so who cares; and besides, in our desperate new world, we can’t afford to instantiate anyone who can’t pull their own weight. What do you think?

questions.heading: Uplifts
questions.primer: In the decades before the Fall, the science came about to uplift the intelligence of animals (at least, the higher-order animals that already possessed massive amounts of brainpower) to sapience. Most inner-system polities refuse to recognize Uplifts as legally equal to humans, even if there’s no denying they’re as sapient as humans. Many consider them property of the entity that created them; the Jovian Junta views them as an abomination and has any that come within its borders put to death. Perhaps as a result, Mercurials are often radical Uplifts-rights champions, and most everyone out-system agrees that Uplifts are people, too.

questions.heading: AGIs and other infolife
questions.primer: Artificial General Intelligence - predating the Fall by a good long while out of fears of exactly what happened, an AGI is a synthetic (info)lifeform, with its capacity for self-improvement hobbled to be similar to transhuman learning, and usually (though not always) socialized in human cultures from the moment its program began to run. In much of the solar system and beyond, AGIs are illegal, subject to summary deletion when captured; other places see this as abhorrent on the scale of a war crime. Where do you stand?

questions.heading: Neotenics
questions.primer: There are some good, rational, logical explanations to be made as regards the utility of Neotenic bodymorphs - in space they’re often more efficient, as brute strength is seldom necessary (and can be provided by a drone when it is). Meanwhile, they provide a biomorph that doesn’t require as many resource inputs, is smaller and thus requires less living space and generally less resources for its equipment, and so on and so forth. Other people simply find them comfortable. That said, let’s not beat around the bush and talk about something nearly everybody would admit about neotenics -- barring those in denial deeper than Jupiter’s gravity well, those concealing something, or the outside chance that someone somehow remained innocent enough not to have thought of it: Neotenic morphs are used by some as a slightly more socially acceptable outlet for pedophilia. Some find this as heinous as clear-cut cases of child sexual abuse; others would argue that if the ego in the morph is old and experienced enough to give informed consent, the size and shape of the morph is immaterial.

questions.heading: Mercurialism
questions.primer: Not, strictly speaking, the simple conglomeration of Uplifts and Infolife, the Mercurial cause is that of those who wish to be as different from baseline transhumanity as possible. Mercurial Uplifts don’t simply want uplifts to be treated as equal to transhumanity, they wear on their sleeve the fact that they are fundamentally different. The mercurial cause incorporates radical uplift and AGI rights activists, as well as some forms of Brinker which are becoming something entirely unalike to transhumanity. The most radical Mercurials actively resist any offers or efforts to assimilate them into “normal” transhuman societies, even those in which they are considered fully equal as all sapient beings, preferring instead to spurn transhumanity altogether in favor of attempting to forge a place for themselves which does not include transhumanity at all.

questions.heading: Hedonism
questions.primer: Almost everybody has an appreciation for having a good time, and almost everybody has some form of a work ethic. Some folk, on the other hand, push these to one extreme or another: most Scum will tell you that they don’t feel like doing anything productive more than what they absolutely have to do to maintain their habitats, and that transhumanity should simply focus on enjoying themselves until the heath-death of the universe. Workaholics sneer at true hedonists, calling them lazy or self-indulgent, and believe that a transhuman should constantly be working, whether to better their own lot in life or to the betterment of all. Where do you stand on this?

questions.heading: Isolationism or Interventionism?
questions.primer: Wherever you stand on the political spectrum, you have to have a point of view on this. This isn’t about your opinions on others’ stances on this matter, as it can safely be said that anyone would prefer those with differing political views to themselves to not be interventionist: this is about your view on your political side, and whether you think they should isolate themselves, or actively interfere in the workings of others opposed to your political bloc.

questions.heading: Technoprogressivism
questions.primer: Not even the staunchest technoprogressive can deny that without modern technology, the Fall would not have happened. A lot of people these days have an uneasy feeling that transhumanity may be playing with technology that it can’t control, and out-of-control technology is dangerous. You don’t have to be a full-on Jovian to feel at least a little bit of fear as regards science blindly rushing forward. On the other hand, others would say that technology isn’t inherently dangerous or evil, and if not misused, is no more harmful than a flashlight. Where do you stand?

questions.heading: Suicide
questions.primer: The Fall was traumatic, and a lot of things in the past ten years have been as well. For whatever their reasons, some people don’t want to deal with existence anymore, and would sooner check out than continue to exist in a state of fear or misery or pain.  On the other hand, we've barely recovered from the near knockout punch that was the Fall.  Immediately after the Fall, in AF 0, humanity’s biologically instantiated population numbered less than 1% of what it had been 18 months before the Fall, and even accounting for infugees, including those in cold storage, transhumanity is still at just 8% of the wholly unique individual minds we once had.  Under those sort of circumstances, some would argue that people don’t have the right to self-terminate and by doing so, diminish the species.

questions.heading: Inflicted Permanent Death
questions.primer: Some people, you just can’t seem to coexist with, whether they’ve done things that offend you to the point of being willing to end them (either out of retribution or to make sure they can’t do it again), or because they’ve taken such a shine to screwing with you that killing them off for good seems like the only way to get them off your back. Of course, everything said above in 6.2i as regards the population of Transhumanity having been nuked (literally and figuratively) down to the single-digit percentile is still true. Transhumanity is an endangered species; given that, do you think it’s permissible to permanently erase a transhuman ego from the galaxy? If so, under what circumstances?

questions.heading: Security, or Liberty?
questions.primer: A revered man at a pivotal era in pre-transhuman history once said, “They who would give up essential liberty, to purchase a little temporary safety, deserve neither liberty nor safety.” Of course, Benjamin Franklin didn’t live in a time in which a lone person operating in secrecy could, with a little determination, annihilate entire habitats. Where do you stand on the scale of liberty and security?

questions.heading: Resleeving
questions.primer: Resleeving - the ability to transfer your consciousness between bodies - has essentially reinvented society. These days, most folks have resleeved at least once, most likely to escape the Fall. What are your thoughts on the whole process? Do you see it as a useful tool, or just a murder box that kills whoever uses it, before printing out a fake copy? Do you see it as an affront to the natural order? Do you avail yourself of every opportunity you get to resleeve?

questions.heading: Indefinite Lifespans
questions.primer: It’s quite possible that the previous generation is the last generation to die (of natural causes). Nowadays, aging is a non-issue, and recovery from even death is perfectly possible. We have entered the age of the immortal. Do you see this as a good thing, or are you one of those folks that asks “who really wants to live forever?” Are you worried that this will ensure that an immortal elite will rule over a perpetually locked-in-place underclass? Or are you simply more concerned with all the things that could nonetheless kill people off?

questions.heading: Forking
questions.primer: When most folks who are now forty or more chronological years old  were children, they were told the same thing that children had been told for hundreds of years: that they were unique. Special, in some way, that nobody else could be. They were lied to: the transhuman brain is understood to a deep enough extent that we can rebuild someone’s mind and personality from whole-cloth gray matter. The reasons a person might do this are innumerable; some might prefer to send a (pruned) fork to a far-off place to hold a conversation in their place, then bring it back and reintegrate it with themselves. Some might spin off a fork to handle purely electronic actions as an infolife. Some just want the company of the one person who knows them best. How many of “you” being out there, active, are you comfortable with? Do you feel there should be a limit on the number of forks of a single person? How does it feel to realize that you can be copied, pasted, or deleted, with a computer command?

questions.heading: Psi and Asyncs
questions.primer: While it might sound improbable to many, the TITANs (themselves improbable) bestowed upon some individuals the ability to manipulate their own mind and others’ minds using sheer force of will. One could be forgiven for thinking they don’t exist, though: this knowledge is actively suppressed by many of the major polities, especially in the inner system - and most asyncs actively try to blend in, or at least keep their use of psi subtle. Opinions are split among those who know - is psi a gift bestowed upon the lucky, or are asyncs little better than TITAN puppets in waiting? Or are you absolutely sure that all that Psi hogwash is nothing but malarkey?

questions.heading: What about the folks you know?
questions.primer: With the proliferation of the social networks, it’s easy to use your rep score to find someone who meets your needs when you’re looking for something specific, be it someone to help you move furniture or help you move a body, be it someone with special expertise or someone looking to take a half-hour’s break out of their day to have sex with a well-recommended stranger. Even so, there are going to be constants in almost everyone’s life - their direct friends and family, their colleagues and recurrent acquaintances. Who are yours?

questions.heading: There is something unique about everyone.
questions.primer: What separates you, specifically, from any hypothetical generic person who has the exact same skill-set and equipment you have?

questions.heading: I know you gave me some serious answer for 8.
questions.primer: Probably some kind of boilerplate thing that you would have put on your C.V. What really makes you unique, what weirdnesses do you have? Some people like to get into brawls in bars and don’t consider it a good night unless they wake up at least in a healing vat. Some people (grognards, mainly) like to play tabletop RPGs over a simulated table, with simulated pencil and paper and simulated carbonated lemon-lime beverages as manufactured centuries ago. Some people (Titanians, mainly) have turned the political process into a fetish; some may have turned it into a literal fetish. Some people seek to do away with gender, while others think the universe would be a lot better if everybody were sleeved into a morph that lets them explore their gender and sexuality at a whim. What’s really odd about you?

questions.heading: What are your minor motivators?
questions.primer: You can’t take up every cause all the time [literally; the formal rules won’t let you have more than three declared motivations] but people tend to have more than three things in life that are important to them. Aside from your mechanical primary motivations, what causes would you lend aid to if you had the spare time, which would you throw a bone to if it came your way and they could make good use of it? Conversely, what causes get your goat - not enough for you, personally, to risk your stack to harm that cause, but which you will enjoy a sense of satisfaction at seeing misfortune brought to?

questions.heading: Let’s try some rapid-fire questions.
questions.primer: A question will be furnished with little, if any, explanation. Answer as you see fit.

questions.heading: Your morph: describe it.
questions.primer: (Gender, apparent ethnicity if any, general looks, build, etcetera. Any mods from standard.)

questions.heading: How do you typically dress, if you dress?
Family. Do you still have any? Are they still important to you?
What religion, if any, do you follow?
questions.primer: What are your thoughts on religions, both old and new?

questions.heading: Why do you do what you do that you don’t, necessarily, have to do?
What won’t you do, no matter the reward offered or any pressing justification?
Make a short list of things not covered above or below that you like, love, dislike, or hate.
questions.primer: It’s okay to come back to this one to avoid repeating answers.

questions.heading: What is your name?
questions.primer: Your full birth name / designation / et cetera; and any nicknames, street names, and the like, including how you came by those monikers.

questions.heading: What citizenship(s) do you hold, if any?
If you had to pick one person, cause, or group, to name as the one you love the most.
As 11L, only the one you hate the most.
As 11L, only the one you respect the most.
As 11L, only the one you fear the most.
Do you have a favorite color?
questions.primer: It doesn’t necessarily need to be within the ultraviolet spectrum human flats can perceive.

questions.heading: If you eat and/or drink, what’s the best thing you’ve ever had?
questions.primer: This may or may not be identical to asking what is your favorite.

questions.heading: If you had the ability to go any one place in all of the galaxy, where would you go?
questions.primer: Any combination of factors may be in play; limitless credit, reputation, access to Pandora Gates or impossible technologies, the full Reclamation of the Earth; whatever.

questions.heading: What everyday annoyance most gets on your goat?
If you consume any art at all, which is your favorite?
questions.primer: Visual, acoustic, and other, so don’t forget to mention the kind of music you bop to when you’re going about your business.

questions.heading: What is your greatest goal?
questions.primer: If you or forks of you live ten thousand years, what would you, now, like to be able to look back upon in AF 10,010 and say “I did that. It was me. I brought that event/thing/place about.”

questions.heading: What is the greatest, most important thing you have accomplished in your lifetime?
Where did you learn your skills?
Under what circumstances would you betray a confidence or break a promise?
About your Muse…
questions.primer: Almost everybody has one. What’s yours like, how long has it been with you?

questions.heading: When your muse is talking to people other than you (setting up appointments and such) how do they act around others?
What does your Muse generally look like, if they have an avatar at all?
What skills do they have? Are they enhancing your strengths or covering your weaknesses? Both? Neither?
What is the biggest disagreement you've ever had with your muse?
The following questions are about gender, sex, and sexuality; they are optional, but encouraged.
Gender and sexuality are complex in this brave new world.
questions.primer: Transhumans are able to easily and relatively cheaply modify their morph’s sexual characteristics into a form that physically and hormonally matches their internalized gender (or at greater expense have one that was built that way from the start), while other transhumans have gone even further and rejected the idea of gender completely. Some choose to identify as agender, genderless, neutrois (gender neutral), polygender, postgender, gender-fluid, or multi-gender, as well as traditional gender identities from one’s indigenous culture, in addition to binary male and female. This is not referring to the sex of their current morph, but to individual gender identity. With this in mind, what gender are you?

questions.heading: How did you come by your gender identity and sexual characteristics?
questions.primer: Most people are assigned a physical (or electronic) gender when they are born/created, and while most people tend to stick with what they know, some come to realize their internalized gender is more fluid than that simple binary choice. Some undergo a slow and frequently painful realization that their own gender identity doesn’t match the sex/gender they were born with, and may change their physical bodies to match it, change their mental selves to match their morph, or do something else. Some make a conscious choice to try something new and find they like it. How did you come to possess the current combination of internal gender identity and external sexual characteristics you possess?

questions.heading: What gender were you born/created as?
questions.primer: Feel free to skip/delete this one if you were born/created with the gender you presently consider yourself to be.

questions.heading: The true nature of transhuman gender and sex identity can run an almost infinite rainbow.
questions.primer: But in the broad strokes, it can boil down to the following options. What are your opinions of those genders?

questions.heading: Nonbinary genders.
questions.primer: Bigender / polygender including some facet of male, female, or neither; the inhabitants of Winter Hab and their cultural devotees, referred to as “wintered”; genderfluid; etc.

questions.heading: Perhaps you’d answer some questions about sexuality, specifically yours, and your opinions. [No pressure if not; in that case, just delete this section. -Lydia]
How would you describe your sexual orientation, assuming you have one?
questions.primer: If you don’t have a sexual orientation, being completely uninterested in sexuality, please share your opinion on the topic of sexuality itself. It must be interesting.

questions.heading: How flexible are you as regards your orientation?
questions.primer: Can you imagine (voluntary) circumstances that would result in you engaging in sexual behavior outside of your orientation, or do you consider it to be more a hard and fast part of your psyche?

questions.heading: It’s reasonably safe to say that almost nobody can be completely described as “normal,” and never is this more true than in a discussion of their sexuality.
questions.primer: What would you say is true about your personal sense of sexuality that is not true of the majority of transhumanity? This could be your personal kinks/fetishes, or hang-ups, or both.

questions.heading: What are your opinions on orientations that aren’t yours?
questions.primer: Do you have particularly strong feelings about any of them? It wasn’t such a long ago; within living memory, in fact, that human beings were discriminated against, legislated against, persecuted and even lynched for having non-mainstream sexual orientations and preferences.

questions.heading: What are your opinions as regards infolife forms and sexuality?
As long as human beings have had the capability to create art, they’ve been depicting sex.
questions.primer: With XP and simulspace, the variety and intensity of pornography has never been better. Do you have any opinions on the matter?

questions.heading: What are your opinions on sexual relationships?
questions.primer: Is there, in your opinion, an ideal form of relationship, or not? Are you open to the idea of deviating from such a relationship ideal if you meet a/several partners who hold different ideals, or must any prospective partners of yours share your notions of how a relationship should go?

questions.heading: What are your opinions on the matters of love and sexuality and relationships?
questions.primer: Relationships don’t have to involve love, by necessity, but many people still hold an ideal that there should be at least some element of love to an ideal relationship. For that matter, what do you think love is?

questions.heading: Relationships, love, sex, and politics.
questions.primer: These interact in ways that can make for some intriguing social situations, whether personal or writ large in society’s gossip. Need I say more to prompt your next opinion?

questions.heading: Most people wouldn’t express a positive opinion of any of the following things. Still, it’s worth asking your opinions on these matters.
questions.primer: [This set of questions contain content about sexual assault and child sexual abuse, and they are thus moved to the appendix. -Lydia]

questions.heading: Experiences, specifically your own sexual experiences. Interested in sharing? [Again, feel completely free to skip or even delete this section if it doesn’t interest you. -Lydia]
Most people remember their first sexual encounter, for better or for worse.
questions.primer: A lot of people wouldn’t describe it as a particularly positive experience. What would you say was your first time, and what did you think of it?

questions.heading: What’s your sex life like now?
questions.primer: Is it parallel to your love life, separate from it, or do you even have one without the other?

questions.heading: Have you ever tried anything (sexual) you have no more interest in doing?
Is there anything specific you might like to try, but haven’t, either for a lack of partners or social unacceptability?
Have you had any sexual experiences that would be considered extreme or even taboo by large segments of transhumanity, perhaps your own?
questions.primer: If so, was it simply experimental, or has it become a regular part of your sexuality?

questions.heading: Recreation and frivolities
questions.primer: Everyone has some idea of what to do for fun. Excluding your sexual recreation, if you engage in such activities (which will have been exhaustively covered above, if you so chose to share), what do you like to do when nothing else is going on and you just want to waste some time?

questions.heading: Social Entertainment
questions.primer: Even these days, people still like to get together and do things with one another, just for fun. Again, excluding sexual forms of social entertainment, what sort of things do you like to do in physical proximity to others; things like getting together to hear a live performance of music, social dining (as opposed to scarfing your dinner by yourself), in-person gambling, physical or mental competitions (or a combination thereof, like chessboxing), et cetera.

questions.heading: Music
questions.primer: Find someone who doesn’t like music in some form or another, and you have found someone who is an extreme statistical outlier. Whether it’s the work of centuries-old maestros whose music was considered so culturally and historically critical to transhumanity that entire special operations teams laid down their lives to evacuate the originals from Earth during the Fall, to something straight out of the synthcore grind-pop squealie-wheelie synth-box of someone who couldn’t carry a tune in a bucket but is convinced his own music is the most glorious thing to ever vibrate through the air, to even newer and wilder forms of experiencing music such as listening to the background radiation of the universe transcribed as sound and listened to in a medium of pure gaseous sulfur hexafluoride, virtually everybody alive likes something in the way of music, and would probably go nuts if forced to spend more than a few days without the benefit of their tunes.

questions.heading: Electronic Gaming
questions.primer: Distinct from competitions such as sports,  which were in times past referred to as games, as well as from pastimes such as card or board games, let’s talk about gaming.  Video games first became widespread in the late 1980s, and have been going strong ever since. In the first few decades of the 21st century, divisions began to arise, between “True” gaming, the sort that people at the time needed either specialized “console” or “Handheld” purpose-built gaming hardware or powerful personal computers to play, and “Casual” gaming, the sort of which they played on their “Smart” mobile telephones and tablet devices, which can be considered a primitive form of ecto. These days, of course, the mesh inserts in the heads of almost everybody on a small habitat collectively outweigh the entire storage capacity and processing power of the entire electronic world of the early 21st century, but we still tend to either game one of two ways: Either casually, with the sort of entopic AR game you might play to pass time when you’ve nothing better to do, or seriously, with full-immersion simulspace environments the likes of which could literally only be imagined in those days. It’s safe to say that gaming, in some form or another, has almost as much a universal appeal to transhumanity as music does; everyone from hypercorp CEOs to bored teenagers can safely be said to spend at least half an hour of any given day playing a game of some sort, and many people spend a lot more than that. How much do you game, and what sort of games do you like - solo, multiplayer, massively multiplayer; adventure, action, RPG; casual, immersive, somewhere in between?

questions.heading: Non-Interactive Entertainment
questions.primer: As long as there are folks out there with a story to tell and folks who want to experience stories told by others, non-interactive entertainment will remain a thing. Everything from reading a good book to watching a movie to eXperience Playback, non-interactive entertainment other than music is still going strong. Of course, it’s true that these days, the definition of “non-interactive” can be blurred quite a lot; even if the creator didn’t produce alternative tracks, viewpoints, etcetera, your muse is often capable of adaptively editing stories for your consumption. Books are easiest, of course; a good muse you’ve been with a long time can probably put together an entire book custom- tailored to your tastes from whole cloth faster than you can read a single page of it, never mind the ease with which they can modify a text-only story to your liking, whether you simply would prefer the hero of the story to be a heroine instead, or would prefer instead to explore the entire narrative from the designated villain’s point of view. Tailoring a film is trickier, and usually can’t be done on the fly unless the creator has included a significant library of modifications to apply, or others have produced modifications to similar effect; an early example of this would be the fan edits of the Star Wars prequel trilogy which removed a loathed character and can still be found floating around the mesh to this day. Customizing an XP is tricker, though, and at the least typically requires more time, and quite a bit more resources than customizing a movie.

questions.heading: Other hobbies
questions.primer: There are a vast number of things transhumans do as hobbies, excluding the things covered above. Free-running, for instance, has experienced an unprecedented surge in popularity in the decade since the Fall. People still like to make or modify things with their own hands, whether permanent handmade objects of actual utility, to cooking by hand instead of eating a ‘maker-prepared meal directly. Some love to write, others tinker with genetic code for the hell of it. Do you have any hobbies, and if so, what are they?

questions.heading: Skinning
questions.primer: Modern entopic technology allows a person to override reality at will, “skinning” their perceptions of reality in the way that some ancient computer programs would allow you to reskin the user interface. This skinning can be indiscernible from the real thing; your trude down stark metal corridors can be transformed into a pleasant midday stroll down a narrow hedge maze, or you can turn your world into a thunderous hellscape to harmonize with a foul mood for cathartic release. You can enjoy the floral scents of a botanical garden whilst standing literally knee-deep in the habitat’s septic tanks, or turn nutrient paste into something that actually tastes like something you enjoy. You can, of course, share your skins with others, whether it’s simply whatever audio tracks you’re jamming to, or to share the custom skin you’ve spent days working on with all your friends. Or, alternatively, you can use it to censor out parts of reality that you find distressing or aggravating, such as almost never having to observe any evidence that that rotten bastard you’d as soon airlock as talk to still exists.

questions.heading: Drugs
questions.primer: It can be accurately stated that a greater percentage of transhumanity is enjoying a narcotically-induced altered state of consciousness at any given moment now than at any other point in transhumanity’s history. From timeless classics such as alcohol and nicotine to brand-new forms of never-before seen brain-benders that just came off the workbench in the last ten minutes, to knowingly ingesting substances which are lethally toxic (with or without the medichines to prevent the lethality part). What are your preferences?

questions.heading: Astrology and other personality typing
questions.primer: Some people hold that there are only N kinds of people in the world. Do you put stock in astrology, Myers-Briggs types, enneagrams, or any other kinds of personality classification? Do you particularly identify with any such archetype? There are, of course, those who dismiss such things as reductive, inaccurate frivolity; do you count yourself among them?

questions.heading: Let’s talk about emotion and trauma.
questions.primer: Almost nobody in the current total of transhumanity has had a care-free life completely unmarred by stress. Most people have at least one formative experience involving negative emotions - some people are arguably affected to the core of their being, and would otherwise have been completely different. Uncomfortable as it might be, answering about these experiences could paint a more complete picture of your life and your mind.

questions.heading: Have you ever died? Do you remember any of your deaths?
questions.primer: Of course, a decent number of people currently walking around are re-instantiated from cold storage, back from a death during the Fall that they may or may not remember. Some people, like the Jovians, would argue that any time an ego resleeves into a new morph is a death of a mind - but most wouldn’t think to count that as such. Then there are deaths that people register as deaths, and that they remember: if one’s cortical stack is recovered after one dies, it is possible to remember the previous morph shutting down from a first person perspective. Seeing as death is one of the most potent sources of emotional trauma known to transhumanity, it’s not hard to imagine that having experienced a death would change a person’s outlook.

questions.heading: Have you ever killed anyone?
questions.primer: You are, of course, permitted to decline to comment. Even if it just amounts to wrecking someone else’s morph temporarily and setting them back for a while, the standard transhuman mind is wired such that committing violence on someone else involves a lot of stress. Permanently removing someone from existence - inflicting permanent ego death upon them - might be even more stressful, even if it involves a level of deliberation not present in drawing a weapon on them. Participating in the death of another is an experience many would seek to avoid, some receive apathetically or begrudgingly, and a handful embrace.

questions.heading: What is the most afraid you’ve ever been?
questions.primer: Without a doubt, a lot of people were afraid during the Fall. But with new horrors lurking in some under-examined corners of the universe, even the Fall might pale in comparison. Do you care to talk about a particular time that stands out?

questions.heading: What is the most angry you’ve ever been?
questions.primer: Some people anger quickly. Other people might have anger psychosurgically suppressed, if they ever had the capacity in them at all. Then there are some situations when very few people would be able to suppress all signs of an emotional response. On top of that, reactions while angry can be different. Again, does any particular moment seem relevant?

questions.heading: Have you had an experience with personal betrayal?
questions.primer: Defining betrayal is something everyone would do differently, but there are some constants: a feeling of trust in an entity, and the feeling that that trust was disregarded at one’s expense. No matter how the situation plays out or the feeling is induced, it’s never a pleasant experience, and it tends to stick with a person.

questions.heading: What’s the saddest you’ve ever been?
questions.primer: If nothing else, everybody who’s at least ten years old lost somebody during the Fall. While loss is a common cause of sadness, it’s far from the only one: maybe you didn’t get that promotion you wanted, or maybe somebody made an off-hand remark that really hurt your feelings, or maybe you made a mistake that hurt somebody. These moments can leave marks on you, just like fear, anger, and death. Any moments of sadness that stand out?

questions.heading: Exosolar Affairs
questions.primer: Like it or not, Pandora’s Gate yawns open wide. What are your thoughts on the topics of exosolar affairs?

questions.heading: Gatecrashing.
questions.primer: Some people say the Pandora Gates are artifacts of the TITANs evacuation of the solar system and should be left the hell alone. The Factors - the first confirmed alien race humanity made first contact with - gave humanity a stark warning against playing with the gates, which humanity promptly ignored. For better or worse, multiple entities, including the PC’s Pathfinder hypercorp, the ostensibly-neutral Gatekeeper hypercorp, the unaffiliated TerraGenesis hypercorp, the Love and Rage Collective, and the Go-Nin hypercorp, control Pandora Gates in the solar system, and frequently send gatecrashers through the gates. Now, there are several large exosolar colonies of humanity. Do you feel humanity is exposing itself to unnecessary existential risks by playing with the gates, or helping to preserve themselves against a system-wide extinction event?

questions.heading: Exosolar Ecology
questions.primer: Less than ten years ago, transhumanity still didn’t know for certain whether life was an aberration unique to our small blue jewel, or if there was more life out there. Now we know for sure, and we have discovered planets with biospheres, some of them even somewhat habitable to us. Needless to say, a lot of folks are chomping at the bit to exploit those planets for all they’re worth, and others would quite literally just as soon burn someone’s stack as allow them to bend so much as a single blade of alien grass. What’s your stance on the issue?

questions.heading: Alien Affairs
questions.primer:
“Two possibilities exist: Either we are alone in the universe, or we are not. Both are equally terrifying.”
Arthur C. Clarke’s famous quote received its answer in the last decade, when the Factors, a sapient race of predatory fungi, rolled into our solar system. We’ve also uncovered clear and irrefutable proof of other sapient life, in the form of extrasolar ruins - discovered in the ten years since the Fall - that could not have been made by anything but an advanced society, and that distantly predate the Fall itself. Clearly, then, we are not alone. In the centuries before the Fall, humanity at large envisioned making contact with new and unknown life as a wonderful event, the stepping stone to joining a vast interstellar community of races. In the wake of the Fall, however, Transhumanity is exceedingly weak compared to what we were, and the aliens we’ve met have proven to have technology significantly more advanced than our own. This makes a lot of people very nervous.

questions.heading: Most people wouldn’t express a positive opinion of any of the following things.
questions.primer: Still, it’s worth asking your opinions on these matters.

questions.heading: Rape and sexual assault.
questions.primer: Is the state of public education about consent sufficient? With the numerous mind-bending drugs invented in recent years, and with psychosurgery (or even forknapping) a constant possibility, does the advent of new forms of exploitation trouble you?

questions.heading: Impersonation and voyeurism.
questions.primer: What are the ethical implications of duplicating someone’s image in order to have sex with them? Perhaps even their entire morph? Is it no worse than idle fantasy; or worse, perhaps rising even to the level of violating them personally? How about replaying somebody else’s XP of having sex, whether the object of your desire is the XP creator or the other participant?

questions.heading: Bestiality.
questions.primer: Most people would say that sexuality with non-sapient critters is a big no-no, but some would also consider sex with sapient uplifts to be the same - and some uplifts would consider sex with sapients of a different race to be bestiality. On the other hand, literally anybody can sleeve into an uplift body if they want to - does that change the nature of it?

questions.heading: Child sexual abuse and related issues.
questions.primer: The problem of child sexual abuse still exists, as it did in the days before resleeving and genetic engineering. Sexual attraction to children (pedophilia) still also exists, and there are myriad new ways for people to act upon the impulse. These days, a young ego can easily be sleeved into an adult morph, or vice versa. And of course, there’s neotenic morphs, which will reach a maximum apparent maturity of somewhere between the baseline human ages of 10 and 13, in terms of size, build and appearance. What are your thoughts?

questions.heading: What are your thoughts on habitat laws/rules/norms which govern sexuality and sexual practice?
questions.primer: This can be in general, or about those specific to any particular habitat.

questions.heading: Muses: attachment to them, and sexuality around them.
questions.primer: The topic of people forming sexual attachments with their muses can be a hotly debated one at times. On the one hand, most people consider muses to be non-sapient AIs; on the other, a muse can and often is the nearest, dearest, and longest-lasting relationship a person has, more real to them than the vast majority of transhumanity. What do you think?
